newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai A, B shares plunge at close on crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai A, B shares plunge at close on crackdown.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended down 6.362 points or 9.6 percent to 59.929 points on Monday on panic selling triggered by an unexpected crackdown by the central government on the stock markets, traders said.
Shanghai's A share index closed down 115.370 or 9.92 percent at 1,047.68 points also on the crackdown, they said.
Beijing on Monday suddenly announced a crackdown after months of dramatic surges on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock markets.
"All of a sudden, market sentiment plunged to the lowest point since the start of this year," said one trader.
"Panic selling was triggered with nobody wanting to buy even at limit-down prices, making volumes plummeting," he said.
Nearly all shares closed at limit-down.
Combined A share volume fell to 129.5 million shares worth 1.3 billion yuan, from 863.5 million shares worth 9.6 billion yuan last Friday.
B share volume fell to 6.6 million shares worth $2.9 million from 56.4 million shares worth $23.3 million on Friday.

"Investor confidence was totally destroyed," said a second trader. "The index will continue to freefall in the short-term with the B share index likely to breach the historical low at the 45-point level shortly."
